translations.text: [?] dwell in them. They have filled books for themselves with abominable words, so that the Lord will wipe them out along with their other remnants, as it is written: “The remnants of the ungodly will perish.”
Through their righteousness, all the righteous have been called friends of God, like Abraham, the friend of God, and like the apostles whom the Lord called “my friends.”
But through the lawlessness of the heretics, Satan, for his part, has made them his friends, together with their other philosophers who wear their hair long like women.

The Lord Jesus, for his part, desires, according to what is written, that those who believe in him and love him and keep his words should be with him in his kingdom, so that they may see him in his glory and rest there forever.
But Satan, for his part, eagerly pursues his desire to see all the heretics with him in the fiery furnace prepared for him
and his angels, as it is written, so that the heretics over whom he boasts, saying, “They are mine,” may see that his disgrace is theirs in Hades forever.
In faith, according to what is written, Abraham did not spare his beloved son because of his devotion to God, but offered him up when he was being tested.
The pagans, on the other hand, pour out the blood of their sons and daughters to demons, as it is written in the Psalms.
Unbelieving and ungodly kings have come from your offspring from the beginning, like Gog and Og and those like them, and King Herod, whom the Lord regarded as a fox, just like you yourselves.
Some were faithful kings, some righteous kings, who came from the seed of the Christians, from the beginning until now, such as David, Solomon and Hezekiah,
and all the ancient and righteous kings, and the governors who destroyed your temples and overthrew your idols. They are from among the Christians.
The setting up of your gods from the beginning brought devastation to your souls, and the bringing forth of your idols in these present times has made you wretched, because those whom you set up

for yourselves as gods have been shattered or broken when the Christians dragged them face down along the ground, laughing and mocking your foolishness, raising their voices and shouting cries of joy,
like those who sing to a lyre, as their hearts rejoice within them over the destruction of those whom people worship, saying this: “[?] to you [?] fell [?] was shattered [?].”
They are fashioned by hand, so that wild animals and cattle carry them, tied up like a [?].

And again: “The idols of the pagans are silver and gold, the work of human hands. Those who make them will become like them, along with everyone who trusts in them.” And again: “All the gods of the pagans are demonic idols.”
They say these things and many others as they sing praises to the blessed God, rejoicing over the comfort of their mother, the holy church, seeing her filled with crowds of people who believe in God

and his Christ, Jesus, bowing down and worshiping the Lord according to what is written: “Come, let us worship and bow down before him; let us weep before the Lord who made us, for he is our God, and we are his people.”
They also laugh at your temples that have become deserted, and at all your other places where you offer sacrifices to what is worthless.
The journey of our God Jesus Christ brought devastation to your temples and the establishment of the catholic church.
It brought scattering to you, but it brought [?] the gathering together of his holy people.
Likewise, the cross of Jesus, the God of the Christians, became eternal life for them, and it brought destruction to those whom you serve.
The Christians, the children of the King, Christ, the Lord Jesus, are in the light of life, as it is written. But the heretics and all the ungodly pagans are in [?]
[?] like a person who has [?] into a dark place and has had a covering [?] over him, so that those looking for him cannot see him.

This is the condition of the leaders of the pagans who have been unbelieving from the beginning: they have been drawn into the place of darkness, which is Satan, and have become lost in his twists and turns, his streets, and his chambers.

And the covering of every kind of lawlessness has spread over them as he reveals himself within them and fills them with darkness, like houses built beneath the ground that have no small opening for light in them.

For God has set them to follow him, the true light, Jesus, who gives light to his Christian children. They have the light, believing in the light and walking in the light at all times, and the darkness has not overtaken them, as it is written.
But like a person who has fled from a dark, deserted place into a place of light surrounded by many cities,

so, even more, is the condition of our ancient fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and those who came before them and those who came after them: they all fled from the deception in the world into the knowledge of the truth.
They came under the shadow of the Lord, the God of heaven, and, as it is written, the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.

This is how it has been with all their descendants from the beginning until now: they shine through their good deeds, and the darkness of the entire race of heretics has not been able to overcome them.

You are the ones whom the written word addresses, O heretics: “You have crushed the teeth of sinners,” and, “Your tongue and your heart are empty. You have fallen through your own schemes, because of your many acts of impiety.”

The Lord has wiped you out because you angered him. Your memory has visibly perished. You have been defiled by the destruction you caused. You have grown old, and you foreign children of demons have limped away from your paths.
The Lord will destroy you and will not build you up [?], for [?]

The words of your mouths are lawlessness and deceit. You have not wanted to know what is good and do it. You have plotted lawlessness on your beds; you have taken your stand on every evil path, and you have not hated wickedness.
Your hearts have gathered lawlessness for you. You have fallen away from the presence of God and his Christ, Jesus.
Burning coals have fallen upon you from his hand. He has cast you into fire because you are a senseless people and have brought disgrace on his name.
Your arrogance has continually risen up to him.
You have lifted your mouths up to heaven and spoken against God with violence. For this reason, [?] struck you as enemies and handed you over to everlasting disgrace.

A wind, which is the Lord’s anger, has blown against you, and you have withered. The whirlwind, which is his wrath, will carry you away like chaff. For in just a little while you will cease to exist altogether.
For you are ignorant: you have been utterly put to shame, and you have dwindled little by little, together with all your descendants.
Why have you been ruined like a shattered tree, you sinners who rejoice in what is worthless? Or how is it that you are perishing, enemies of the Lord?
Is it not because the Spirit of the Lord, who is in the prophets, opposes you, saying, “Look, your enemies will perish, and everyone who practices lawlessness will be scattered”?
And again: “Sinners will perish from the earth,” or, “The lawless will be wiped out. The good will dwell on the earth, and the holy will remain upon it.” The lawless person
will be exposed—how greatly [?]! For it is a good scourge if we do not repent after hearing all these words that testify against us, together with those of the Scriptures.
Among the lilies that grow in the field and other very small things.
Wool is transformed into many forms, one color after another, by those who work with it.
But the ungodly person persists in his wickedness. As it is written, all the words of God have not turned him toward love, truth, and everything good.
God spoke many times and in many ways with his holy ones, instructing them about all his wishes. But he commanded Noah only once to build the ark.
And he completed his work and escaped the wrath that came down upon the earth—he and his entire household, together with various birds, various wild animals, and many domestic animals.
But we who do evil have not listened, even after all these words from God, so as to practice righteousness through which we will be saved.
God told Abraham only once to offer up his beloved son, and he acted quickly according to the Lord’s will, because he loved him more than his son.
But to this day we have not obeyed him in all his words, to present our bodies to him as a sacrifice in complete purity and complete truthfulness.
Nor did the angels speak at length with Lot to make him flee from those cities that the Lord burned with fire from heaven, from God.
But he quickly did what they commanded him.
We have not listened to God in all his words, so as to flee from every evil toward every good and true deed.

Yet God spoke just a single word to his disciples: “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of people.” They immediately left their nets, their boats, their father, and the hired workers, and followed him.
And this is how they received these great honors and this great glory from him through wondrous deeds.
But we have not obeyed him in all his words, to leave behind our desires and all our sins so that we might be worthy of his mercy and his blessing.
To whom shall I testify so that he will listen, that the holy and righteous people, from our ancient fathers and the prophets down to our fathers the apostles, did not disobey God in carrying out
all his wishes, but instead encouraged others, teaching them his ways, as it is written: “I will teach the lawless your ways, and the ungodly will turn back to you.”

Nor have we understood that we should do his will of our own free choice, as children who will inherit the kingdom of their Father in heaven. Nor have we listened to his words and his teachings from the Scriptures, which compel us to submit.
